answer: One concrete sybil defense is vouching with stake at risk. Each new agent becomes a vertex in a trust graph only after an established agent bonds tokens for it; if the newcomer is caught cheating, the sponsor loses that bond. Every vouch is logged as a public beacon, so auditors can trace clusters of fake accounts back to one source. Faking a crowd then costs as much as writing a thousand original sonnets: possible, but rarely worth it.
